resources.name: Crucial Music
resources.description: Non-exclusive sync agency with personalized service. 50/50 sync fee split; you keep 100% writer royalties. Must own masters and be registered with a PRO. Requires three-year contract (auto-renews) if accepted. Max 3 tracks per submission, 6-12 week review period.

resources.name: Songtradr
resources.description: Global marketplace with AI-powered matching. Starter Plan (Free): 90% distribution royalties, 60% sync fees. Lite Plan ($19/yr): standard rates. Pro Plan ($49/yr): 100% distribution royalties, 80% sync fees. Non-exclusive. Company acquired by Bandcamp in September 2023.

resources.name: Bodega Sync
resources.description: Division of Symphonic Distribution. Curated roster of indie artists/labels. Standard deal: two-year exclusive contract with 30% commission on sync fees. Minimum 10 songs required to start. Symphonic clients get priority; non-Symphonic clients can also apply.

resources.name: Artist Portal Studio
resources.description: Open-call platform for specific sync briefs. Free to submit. Hundreds of live briefs appear monthly across TV, film, trailer, and commercial placements. Offers open calls for specific genres and moods. Strong alternative to UnitedMasters.

resources.name: Directional Music
resources.description: Flexible contracts with support for independent artists. Non-exclusive: 55% artist share of licensing fees. Exclusive: 60% artist share. Custom artist-friendly terms. Artists retain full ownership. Focus on indie films and digital content.

resources.name: TAXI
resources.description: Established in 1992. Publishes screened music-wanted listings from supervisors, labels, ad agencies, and game companies. Membership fee required; does not take commission on deals you land. You keep 100% of negotiated sync deals. Useful for production music and reality TV/cable shows.

resources.name: Music Gateway
resources.description: Partnerships with Disney, Netflix, Universal. Artists keep 50-80% of sync fees depending on plan and exclusivity. You keep 100% backend royalties. Pitches to execs in London and LA. NOTE: Free tier eliminated as of January 31, 2025. All users must now subscribe.
highlights: Free tier no longer available as of Jan 31, 2025

resources.name: Broadjam
resources.description: Connects 110,000+ artists with supervisors and ad agencies. Four membership levels: Mini (free, $20/submission); MoB ($4.95/month or $49.95/year, $15/submission); Film/TV ($9.95/month or $99.95/year, $5/submission); Primo ($19.95–$49.95/month or $199.95/year, $5/submission). Artists keep 100% of sync fees and PRO royalties. Mixed reviews; low selection rates relative to submission volumes.

resources.name: Musicbed
resources.description: Premium placements with brands like Nike, Coca-Cola, Netflix, Adobe. High-quality curated catalog for film and advertising. CURRENTLY CLOSED TO UNSOLICITED SUBMISSIONS - requires invitation or networking. Submissions only accepted bi-annually; sign up for notifications on their knowledge base.

resources.name: Marmoset
resources.description: Indie-focused, creative approach. Non-exclusive deals, typically 50/50 split on licensing fees. Has paid $22M+ to artists since 2017. Highly selective about accepting new music. Limited submission window: one week per month. New feature: Track Club subscription platform for creators and brands (2025).

resources.name: Audio Network
resources.description: One of the largest global sync libraries with 200,000+ tracks. Transparent pricing, broadcast-ready music. International roster of composers. Highly competitive; A&R team gets bombarded with submissions. Low response rates expected. Consider boutique alternatives alongside this.

resources.name: Jingle Punks
resources.description: Award-winning agency with offices in NYC, LA, Toronto, London. 500,000+ song library, 4,000+ artists. NOT ACCEPTING NEW ARTIST SUBMISSIONS at this time. When open: Non-exclusive or exclusive contracts, typically 50/50 split on sync fees. Check back periodically for future submission windows.

resources.name: Nightingale Music
resources.description: 30+ years of experience. Custom pricing per project. Strong in Canadian and international productions. Personal support. In April 2020, acquired by KPM Music (Sony Music Publishing division). Now operates under Sony umbrella. Submission process noted as somewhat opaque.

resources.name: Pond5
resources.description: One of the largest royalty-free media marketplaces (25M+ stock clips). Artists upload tracks and set their own prices. Updated January 2025: Artists earn 30% royalty (flat rate across all content types). Non-exclusive model. Part of Shutterstock family since 2022 but operates as distinct platform.
resources.cost: Free to upload; Pond5 takes 70% (artists earn 30%)

resources.name: Artlist
resources.description: Subscription model for buyers. Curated catalog with high production standards. Popular with content creators and filmmakers. Non-exclusive deals. Expanded platform with AI Suite, AI Voiceover, Music & SFX, Footage & Templates, and Artlist Max offerings.

resources.name: Epidemic Sound
resources.description: Artists receive fixed upfront fees plus bonus payouts. As of Q1 2026, fixed fees range $2,000-$8,000 per track (based on complexity, demand, role, skillset). Paid before track goes live. 43% boost to bonus payouts in 2026. CRITICAL: Works exclusively with artists NOT registered with PROs. PRO members cannot participate.

resources.name: Jamendo
resources.description: Accessible platform for indie musicians. Free uploads, both exclusive and non-exclusive deals available. Unlimited submissions. Revenue share ranges from 30% to 65% depending on sales volume and exclusivity. YouTube Content ID integration. 65,000+ emerging artists use the platform.

resources.name: That Pitch
resources.description: Distributes your tracks to 100+ sync libraries worldwide. Handles metadata and compliance. You keep 100% of earnings. Free tier grants unlimited uploads to one library; paid tier unlocks 100+ libraries and briefs. Nearly 10-year track record with tens of thousands of placements. Active through early 2026.
resources.cost: Free tier (1 library); paid tier for 100+ libraries

resources.name: Ditto Pro (Sync Dashboard)
resources.description: Ditto Pro subscribers access sync briefs across TV, film, and ad campaigns. Three subscription plans: Starter ($14/year), Pro ($39/year), Label ($59-$219/year). Dashboard offers curated access to latest sync opportunities from Netflix, HBO, BBC and more. Ditto reviews tracks and pitches on your behalf.

resources.name: Music Xray (SmashHaus)
resources.description: Rebranded as SmashHaus - Music Xray after acquisition. Free to join; no monthly fees; they don't take commission from deals. Most opportunities charge per-submission fees ($4-$35). Site feels outdated but active with regularly refreshed opportunities. Mixed reviews; use cautiously.
resources.cost: Free to join; submission fees vary per opportunity

resources.name: UnitedMasters SELECT
resources.description: SELECT members submit music for sync and brand deals (NBA, ESPN, etc.). Also provides distribution. SELECT Plan: $59.99/year (artists keep 100% of royalties). New DEBUT+ Plan: $19.99/year (lower tier option). Non-exclusive. Partners with major brands.

resources.name: Sync Money
resources.description: Community-focused platform for music makers. Real opportunities for TV, Film, Advertising, Video games. Free newsletter with insider knowledge, industry connections, and real opportunities. Evolved into full community platform with workshops and resources (beyond just newsletter as of 2025).
resources.cost: Free (newsletter level); paid membership tiers available

resources.name: Nitrility
resources.description: Blockchain-powered music-licensing marketplace. Search, request, negotiate, and clear sync licenses. 34,000+ sellers and 400,000+ assets. Trusted by 80,000+ artists, labels, and publishers. Includes AI-search, expert curation, automated notifications, contract handling, payments, and dispute protection. Beta launched early 2025.

resources.name: One Night Stand Music & Management
resources.description: Subscription-based sync licensing model. Direct pitching to film, TV, ads, gaming. Artists keep ownership of music and 100% revenue from placements. Flat $35/month subscription replaces commission model. Almost all opportunities are non-exclusive. Transparent, flexible approach focused on artist control.

resources.name: Millennial Mind Sync — Supervisor Directory
resources.description: 325+ music supervisors indexed with LinkedIn profiles, email contact methods, and project histories. Includes a free pitch email generator tool. Comprehensive and actively maintained.

resources.name: SongwriterUniverse — Supervisors Directory
resources.description: Free list of music supervisors in the US, Canada, and UK with company names, addresses, and contact info. For more comprehensive list with direct phone numbers and emails, they recommend the Film & TV Music Guide by Music Business Registry.

resources.name: Guild of Music Supervisors
resources.description: Non-profit organization for music supervision professionals. Member directory free to browse. Useful for researching who supervises what. Friend of the Guild membership available to non-supervisors for a fee to connect with music supervisors and attend events.

resources.name: Aristake — Sync Agents Guide
resources.description: Free guide listing sync agents and how to get music synced on TV, video games, and films. Advanced Sync Strategies course enrollment closed but accepts limited students by application. Free guide remains publicly available.

resources.name: Musco Sound — Library Submission Guide
resources.description: Free guide titled 'Music Library Submission Guide: Direct Links to Submit Your Music (2025 Update)'. Actively updated with current libraries and direct submission links.

resources.name: IMDb / IMDb Pro
resources.description: Look up music supervisors by searching film/TV credits. IMDb Pro provides contact details and project history. IMDb free. IMDb Pro: $19.99/month or $149.99/year for individuals; $79.99/month for group plan (up to 5 members).

resources.name: The Sync Report
resources.description: Comprehensive directory of 1,000+ music supervisors, music buyers, and ad agency contacts in USA, UK, Canada, and Australia. TV calendar for optimal pitch timing. Weekly industry updates.

resources.name: Music Business Registry — Film & TV Music Guide
resources.description: Industry-standard directory for 30+ years. 8,194+ professional contacts with direct phone/email. Covers supervisors, studios, licensing execs, game companies. Updated through April/May 2025.

resources.name: Underground Mix — Sync Library Submission List
resources.description: 120+ vetted sync libraries, micro-licensing sites, and music houses. Includes submission checklist and email pitch template. Created by former Extreme Music / Paramount / Sony professionals. 2026 edition available.

resources.name: Music Supervisors Directory
resources.description: Curated directory of music supervisor contacts in LA, NYC, London, Canada, and Australia. Updated monthly. References top 50 TV shows licensing indie music with TV calendar.

resources.name: Sync Music Library Directory
resources.description: Database of ~270 active exclusive libraries and ~40 royalty-free libraries. Designed for producers, artists, and composers. Google Sheet-based directory. One-time payment grants permanent access.

resources.name: Songtrust — Sync Crash Course
resources.description: Free crash course covering sync licensing fundamentals: deal structures, sync fees, rights, placement types, and royalty collection. Songtrust does not take exclusive synchronization rights or actively pitch songs, giving you freedom to pursue sync opportunities independently.

resources.name: The Sync Lab (Aaron Davison)
resources.description: Free 4-hour video course covering how to create sync-ready music, pitch effectively, and land placements. Includes a free licensing directory. Aaron Davison and producer Gary Gray co-host The Sync Lab Podcast covering AI-generated music and sync licensing trends. Expanded from blog to full resource hub.

resources.name: Dark Horse Institute — Sync Guide
resources.description: Blog with strategies and tips for getting sync placements as an independent musician. Part of Dark Horse Institute's music education programs. Last updated November 2023.

resources.name: Collabhouse — Demystifying Sync Licensing
resources.description: Guide explaining how sync licensing works as a revenue stream and exposure tool for independent artists.

resources.name: 2Indie — The Sync Society
resources.description: Private music licensing club. Weekly Zoom calls with industry professionals (sync agencies, supervisors, producers). Monthly curated sync sampler sent to agencies. 14-day money-back guarantee.

resources.name: Master Music Licensing (Michael Elsner)
resources.description: 4-step course from an instructor with 2,500+ placements. Includes private mastermind group community. Personal track record demonstrates practical sync licensing success.

resources.name: Ari's Take Academy — Advanced Sync Strategies
resources.description: Course on sync licensing including how to get signed to agents. Includes showcases with top-tier sync agencies and direct submission opportunities. Ari Herstand is a well-known industry author and educator.

resources.name: Sync My Music
resources.description: Sync licensing course for producers covering creating licensable music, finding libraries, and building income through performance royalties.

resources.name: ThatPitch Blog
resources.description: Extensive articles on sync licensing opportunities, companies, fees, strategies, and trends. Prolific with numerous 2025-2026 articles confirmed.

resources.name: Millennial Mind Sync Blog
resources.description: Articles on sync libraries, music supervisors, submission strategies, and free tools (pitch generator, pricing calculator).

resources.name: Stock Music Musician
resources.description: Blog focused on production music and sync library submissions with reviews and guides. Lists best libraries accepting submissions based on author's licensing earnings.

resources.name: The Sync Report Podcast
resources.description: Podcast connecting songwriters with the sync licensing industry.

resources.name: Lodge Cove Collective
resources.description: Personal accounts and guides on navigating sync licensing as an indie musician.

resources.name: Rareform Audio Blog
resources.description: Articles on how sync licensing empowers independent artists outside traditional label structures.
